paras: NOTE: If it is not medically safe, or if you are panic stricken, sleep deprived, nauseated, deeply destabilized, manic, psychosis like, or chemically overwhelmed, do all you can to stabilize and then ask for what your subconscious needs you to know. It is not ready for you to know if you need to destabilize to know what it is! Ask for capacity and not content!

What to do if your Subconscious Mind Knows Something You Don’t Want to Know. It may have to do with your sexuality, a grief, trauma, family issue, betrayal, shame, vocation, relationship, medical issue, spirituality, addiction, identity, moral issue, or whatever.
Don’t bully your subconscious mind into telling you what it is by saying things like:
Why won’t you just tell me? What are you hiding? Tell me right now! I command you to tell me what it is!

This usually leads to flooding, panic, false certainty, confabulation, dissociation, and a really, really bad day. If you are flooded, then you can’t use your adult capacities to be able to consider different options, to reality test, to plan, to choose differently. Work on your regulation and get support before proceeding. The subconscious may be silent until your Adult is able to regulate, get support, be humble, and proceed in a way that does not blow your Adult out of the water. Ask the parts what they need for your Adult to be able to know what it is:

Do I need to know what it is, or do I need to work on capacity? What can be done to make my conscious mind 5% better at knowing what it is? Can you tell me what it is in a symbolic way without full revelation? Can you tell me what to do to be safe without telling me what it is? Do you need me to get support in order for you to tell me what it is? If so, what kind of support? Who can I go to?

Consider saying: “Dear Subconscious Mind, you are wise and you know things that my conscious mind is not able to know yet. Please don’t rip the bandage off. Prepare my conscious mind to know what it is in a safe way. Ground me before showing me a memory. Support me before turning up the intensity. Tell me what to do next so that I can be ready for what you want me to know.”

REMEMBER: Just because you see something in a hypnotic state does not mean that it is literally true, especially when it comes to traumatic memories. The mind often makes images that are meaningful to you, but are symbolic. It often squashes several things together, distorts, dramatizes, and pulls from cultural sources. Just because you see it, doesn’t mean it’s true. Get support outside to help you!
